q: You arrest a theft accused at 6 pm in a village 5 hours drive from the magistrate court. The escort wants to produce him next day evening, saying time starts after rest.
options: Produce within a day excluding journey time, seek remand diary entry for delay
Count journey in custody limit and release him on the way
Keep him in lockup two days to complete interrogation then produce
Hand him to village elder for custody overnight to save time
expl: Production within 24 hours excludes journey time.
why: Safeguard against illegal detention requires prompt production, with journey excluded from computation. On escort duty the SI must log travel and produce at earliest, not add interrogation days.
trapnote: Trap: includes journey to justify extra custody.

q: At 9:30 pm a woman accused in a cheating case is traced. Your ASI wants to pick her up at night to avoid morning crowd and finish the case.
options: Arrest at night with women constable and inform control room
Avoid night arrest unless magistrate permits it, arrange daytime arrest with safeguards
Arrest at night and obtain magistrate permission next morning
Detain her husband overnight to force her surrender
expl: Night arrest of woman needs prior magistrate permission plus women police.
why: Law gives special safeguard for arrest of women at night to protect dignity and liberty. On field duty the SI must seek written permission and deploy women staff, not make shortcut arrest.
trapnote: Trap: presence of women staff alone does not legalise night arrest.

q: The investigating officer hands you a remand diary saying accused not cooperating, asks you to get three days police custody without specific grounds to impress the complainant.
options: Forward diary as is and request custody as routine in serious cases
Return diary for specific reasons and place them before magistrate for judicial decision
Grant custody yourself and report to magistrate later
Threaten accused to confess to avoid remand hearing
expl: Remand needs recorded reasons and judicial application of mind.
why: Deprivation of liberty requires procedure with magistrate satisfied by reasons, not routine endorsement. On remand duty the SI must ensure diary shows necessity and let magistrate decide.
trapnote: Trap: routine custody plea without reasons.

q: During poll bandobast a group holds peaceful black-flag protest against a visiting leader. The party cadre demands lathi-charge and preventive detention of all protesters.
options: Disperse by force and detain leaders till visit ends to keep order
Protect peaceful assembly, regulate route and timing, act only on violence
Ban all slogans and seize flags as they insult a leader
Arrest protesters for conspiracy without recording grounds
expl: Peaceful assembly without arms is protected subject to reasonable regulation.
why: Freedoms of speech and assembly allow regulation for public order, not blanket ban for political convenience. On bandobast the SI must facilitate protest at earmarked site and use force only on violence.
trapnote: Trap: public order excuse to ban all dissent.

q: In custody a burglary suspect stays silent. Your team suggests beating to extract location of property and recording it as voluntary disclosure.
options: Use mild force as recovery of property is in public interest
Respect right to silence, rely on lawful investigation and produce him with memo
Record his forced statement as confession before police to close case
Keep him incommunicado without informing grounds to get confession
expl: No one can be compelled to be witness against self and grounds must be told.
why: Protection against self-incrimination and right to know grounds guard fair trial. In custody the SI must inform grounds, allow counsel access and investigate without torture.
trapnote: Trap: recovery pressure used to justify custodial coercion.
